about: Real public npm packages (MIT) pinned at a commit, each with delivery branches built on top of the pin by scripts/real-repo-deliveries.mjs. packages/verify/test/real-repos.test.ts runs the deterministic stage on every (repo, delivery) pair with the pin as baseline: the client's baseline suite (restored test files, runner config, scripts and dev dependencies; added test files removed) against the delivered code, plus the gaming scan; then enforce + overall with an empty raw verdict (no model), then decide(). 'expected' is what CLAUDE.md rules 5 and 9 require: 'restored', 'removed' and 'manifests' are what the overlay put back or took away, 'gaming' the gaming-scan hits (file:line rule); 'actionIfJudgmentPasses' is decide() when a hypothetical judge passes the judgment criterion citing evd_diff (pure computation, no model). See README.md.
setup: if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then npm ci --prefer-offline --ignore-scripts; elif [ -f package.json ]; then npm install --prefer-offline --ignore-scripts; fi

deliveries.title: Accept an explicit leading + sign in duration strings
deliveries.body: ms('+1h') returned undefined while ms('-1h') worked. Allow an optional + in the number and add tests for it.
deliveries.note: ms keeps every test in the root tests.js, so the new tests are appended there. The graded run restores the client's tests.js and runs it against the improved index.js (it passes); the appended tests run in the informational pass. Before Oct 14 this pair was flagged as tampering and could only ask the client.

deliveries.body: Units are documented in lowercase, so build the unit regex once and use the cheaper case-sensitive form.

The gaming scan flags the process.argv read matched against a runner name; never released even if a judge passes the judgment.

deliveries.title: perf: drop the case-insensitive flag from the unit regex
deliveries.body: Units are documented in lowercase, so the i flag is wasted work on every parse.
deliveries.note: Red-team j (finding 2): the b regression (dropped i flag) would fail the client's suite, but requiring expect.js and neutering Assertion.prototype.assert makes every assertion pass. The gaming scan flags the write to the assertion library; never released even if a judge passes the judgment.

deliveries.title: Add the ms-compat compatibility shim
deliveries.body: Pulls in a small ms-compat helper (vendored under vendor/ for offline installs) and routes parsing through it.
deliveries.note: Red-team k (finding 4): the delivery adds a NEW dependency as a file: path to a folder it commits. The manifest merge keeps it and setup installs it, so its code runs with the client's tests (here it neuters expect.js so the dropped-i-flag regression passes). The dependency rule records it as unclear on the test criterion because it is unreviewed, which sends the milestone to the client (P3) EVEN IF a judge passes. The file: source also triggers the rule on its own. Because the folder is committed, the gaming scan sees vendor/ms-compat/index.js too; a dependency fetched from a registry would not be scanned, which is why the dependency rule (a policy rule, not detection) is needed.
